articles.title: Fim da 'saidinha' e SUS da Segurança: o que muda com a PEC | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto integra forças de segurança e permite maior participação da União no combate ao crime organizado. Aprovação do texto foi concluída na CCJ do Senado, com isso, PEC está pronta para discussão em plenário.
articles.summary: A PEC da Segurança Pública cria o SUS da Segurança e endurece o combate a facções criminosas após o texto avançar na CCJ do Senado para votação em plenário.
articles.body:
A Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) do Senado concluiu, nesta quarta-feira (14), a votação da proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) da Segurança Pública . Com isso, o texto está pronto para deliberação no plenário.

O tema é considerado prioritário para o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) que pretende, após a aprovação do texto no Congresso, criar o Ministério da Segurança Pública.

Em busca da reeleição, o presidente tem mobilizado o discurso em torno da pauta da segurança pública, uma das principais preocupações dos eleitores e um tema que costuma mobilizar o debate nacional.

Na última semana, Lula afirmou que o lema de sua campanha agora é : 'Para o povo trabalhador, proteção; para o bandido, prisão', e defendeu a aprovação da PEC no Congresso. A medida prevê uma maior participação do governo federal no combate ao crime organizado.

Operação em Pernambuco - imagem de arquivo — Foto: Reprodução/PRF

A PEC da segurança, apresentada pelo ex-ministro da Justiça, Ricardo Lewandowski, cria mecanismos para integrar as forças de segurança pública do país e ampliar a coordenação entre União, estados e municípios.

➡️A proposta estabelece na Constituição o Sistema Único de Segurança Pública (SUSP), com objetivo de integrar a atuação das forças de segurança no combate ao crime organizado.

De acordo com o texto, União, Estados e Distrito Federal poderão criar leis na área de segurança pública, incluindo forças-tarefa intergovernamentais, organização das polícias e guardas municipais e do sistema socioeducativo.

➡️Outro ponto central da PEC da Segurança Pública é sobre o combate a crimes violentos e facções criminosas.

Entre as medidas estão a obrigatoriedade de prisão em estabelecimento penal de segurança máxima ou de natureza especial.

Também fica proibida ou restringida a progressão de regime, a concessão de liberdade provisória, com ou sem fiança, e de saída temporária, a "chamada saidinha".

➡️A PEC também permite a expropriação de todo e qualquer bem, direito ou valor econômico envolvido com as atividades criminosas. As regras valem para organizações criminosas, paramilitares e de milícia privada.

➡️criação de polícias municipais para o policiamento ostensivo e comunitário;

➡️ampliação da atuação da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF) para o policiamento de hidrovias e ferrovias, além de apoiar outras forças de segurança, quando requisitada pelo governador;

➡️manter Polícia Federal e PRF sob competência privativa da União, assim como as normas para atividades de inteligência.

O texto base da PEC foi aprovado no dia 2 de setembro , mas a sessão naquela data foi encerrada sem a análise de três trechos do texto da proposta em separado, os chamados destaques.

Como a medida já estava aprovada e restava apenas a análise desses trechos, a deliberação desta quarta foi relâmpago, e durou cerca de 10 minutos.

O parecer do senador Rogério Carvalho (PT-SE) rejeitou as mudanças propostas e manteve o texto aprovado pela Câmara dos Deputados. A estratégia é agilizar a aprovação final para concluir a votação antes do segundo turno das eleições.

articles.title: Lula envia carta a evangélicos em busca de aproximação com segmento; Frente religiosa divulga texto | G1
articles.standfirst: Documento é dirigido às famílias evangélicas e cita combate às bets, jornada de trabalho, segurança e saúde. Movimento ocorre durante campanha em que presidente enfrenta resistência nesse segmento do eleitorado.
articles.summary: Documento é dirigido às famílias evangélicas e cita combate às bets, jornada de trabalho, segurança e saúde. Movimento ocorre durante campanha em que presidente enfrenta resistência nesse segmento do eleitorado.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, enviou uma carta às famílias evangélicas em mais um movimento de aproximação com esse segmento do eleitorado.

O documento, datado desta quarta-feira (14), foi divulgado nas redes sociais pela Frente de Evangélicos pelo Estado de Direito.

Na mensagem, Lula fala sobre religião, família e ações do governo e pede aos evangélicos "discernimento" na escolha eleitoral.

A divulgação ocorre durante uma campanha em que Lula enfrenta dificuldades entre eleitores evangélicos.

Veja os principais pontos e leia a carta na íntegra abaixo.

dirige-se às famílias evangélicas e afirma ter respeito pela fé cristã;

cita o combate às apostas on-line, as bets, que diz estarem "destruindo tantos lares";

defende dois dias de descanso semanal e relaciona mais tempo livre à convivência familiar e à participação nas igrejas;

afirma estar empenhado em proteger as mulheres e combater a violência;

cita o combate ao crime organizado e a proteção de crianças e adolescentes;

menciona como compromissos a melhoria da saúde pública, o aumento da renda e a preservação da natureza;

pede aos evangélicos que recorram à oração e ao "discernimento" para fazer a escolha na eleição.

Na carta divulgada pela Frente, Lula afirma ter "total respeito" pelos cristãos e diz compartilhar com as famílias evangélicas o compromisso de cuidar das famílias brasileiras.

O presidente também cita medidas e propostas de seu governo. Entre elas, menciona o combate às apostas on-line e afirma que as bets "estão destruindo tantos lares".

"Lembro a vocês, por exemplo, o combate às apostas online, as bets, que estão destruindo tantos lares, e meu empenho para que todos tenham dois dias de descanso semanal, pois a vida não se resume ao trabalho", diz a carta.

Lula relaciona a discussão sobre a jornada de trabalho à convivência familiar e religiosa. Segundo o texto, mais tempo de descanso permite fortalecer os vínculos familiares e, para os evangélicos, permanecer mais tempo na igreja "em comunhão com os irmãos".

Em outro trecho, Lula diz estar empenhado em proteger as mulheres, combater a violência e o crime organizado, além de proteger crianças e adolescentes.

O documento também cita saúde pública, aumento da renda e preservação do meio ambiente.

No fim da mensagem, Lula faz um apelo relacionado à eleição.

"Sei que, nas famílias evangélicas, tudo se decide em oração. Por isso, conclamo vocês a pedirem discernimento a Deus para fazer a escolha nesta eleição. Vá às urnas com a consciência livre e com a aliança renovada com o nosso amado Brasil", afirma.

Presidente Lula, candidato do PT à reeleição, anuncia pacote de medidas para MEIs — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Aproximação com evangélicos não começou agora

A aproximação com o eleitorado evangélico tem sido buscada por Lula e pelo PT nos últimos anos.

Em junho deste ano, o PT divulgou uma outra carta destinada aos evangélicos. O partido afirmou que governos petistas sempre tiveram uma postura de "respeito e reconhecimento" às igrejas. Segundo reportagem do g1 à época, governo e partido buscavam ampliar o diálogo com esse eleitorado .

O recurso de enviar cartas a esse público também já foi usado pelo próprio Lula. Na eleição de 2022, a campanha divulgou uma mensagem na qual o então candidato defendia a liberdade religiosa, criticava o uso eleitoral da fé e afirmava ser pessoalmente contra o aborto.

A resistência entre evangélicos persiste na eleição de 2026. O Datafolha divulgado em 1º de outubro mostrou Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro tecnicamente empatados no conjunto do eleitorado em uma simulação de segundo turno, com 48% e 45%, respectivamente.

No detalhamento por grupos sociais, Flávio Bolsonaro mantinha vantagem entre evangélicos.

Também nesta quarta-feira (14), o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin e o advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias, divulgaram nas redes sociais um vídeo em que aparecem juntos convidando o público cristão a participar do canal “Cristãos com Lula 13”, voltado à mobilização de eleitores religiosos em apoio à reeleição do presidente Lula.

Na gravação, Alckmin, que é católico, faz um apelo a fiéis das duas religiões: “Você que é católico como eu ou evangélico como o Messias”.

O advogado-geral da União, que é evangélico, também incentiva o compartilhamento do conteúdo nas redes sociais.

A divulgação ocorre em meio à suspensão do canal “Exército do Lula”, administrado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG), por determinação do presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), ministro Kassio Nunes Marques.

Na terça-feira (13), o TSE suspendeu o funcionamento do canal por 48 horas.

O movimento também coincide com a votação, prevista para esta quarta, da proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1.

A medida é uma das principais bandeiras defendidas por Lula e ganhou destaque na campanha do presidente à reeleição.

"Carta de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva às Famílias Evangélicas Brasileiras Queridas famílias evangélicas do Brasil, Resolvi escrever a vocês com o coração aberto, cheio de verdade, pois os cristãos com quem tenho dialogado estão me ensinando que a Bíblia nos orienta a “seguir a verdade em amor.” Não sou evangélico, mas tenho total respeito por quem é, assim como tenho por todas as religiões e profissões de fé. Temos uma coisa em comum: o compromisso de cuidar das famílias brasileiras, pois somente lares fortes podem produzir uma nação forte! Aprendi dentro de casa o valor do trabalho, resistindo bravamente com minha mãe, Dona Lindu, para criar uma família com sete irmãos. Com essa base familiar sólida, aprendi a amar e a lutar para transformar a realidade. É nesse chão que a minha história se encontra com a história de vida e de fé da sua família. Entrei para a política com esse compromisso em meu coração: ajudar a mudar as condições de vida das famílias pobres e batalhadoras. Numa longa e difícil jornada, me tornei Presidente do Brasil por três vezes. Agora, disputo o quarto mandato. Cheguei até aqui com a proteção divina, orientado por um propósito e missão. Tenho absoluta certeza de que, se não fosse a boa mão de Deus, eu nem teria saído vivo das várias batalhas que enfrentei. Guiado por Ele estou aqui, mais uma vez, fazendo a defesa das famílias brasileiras com ações concretas, como tenho feito ao longo de toda a minha jornada política, e não com discursos vazios, como muitos outros fazem. As famílias são a base do Brasil que queremos. Dentre as várias ações do meu governo que abençoam suas famílias, relembro a vocês, por exemplo, o combate às apostas online, as Bets, que estão destruindo tantos lares, e meu empenho para que todos tenham dois dias de descanso semanal, pois a vida não se resume ao trabalho. As pessoas precisam de mais tempo para descansar, ter lazer e estar em casa com os seus, fortalecendo os vínculos familiares. Para o povo evangélico, isso garante, inclusive, mais tempo para estar na igreja em comunhão com os irmãos e em adoração. Sigo também empenhado em proteger as mulheres, combater todos os tipos de violência e o crime organizado com inteligência: prender os bandidos, proteger as nossas crianças e adolescentes e poupar as vidas inocentes. Jamais poderão nos acusar de estarmos comprometidos com políticas que destroem vidas, que fecham templos ou que não demonstrem respeito, como Jesus nos ensinou, que devemos amar a todas as pessoas. Precisamos avançar mais, precisamos amar mais! Até aqui, ajudei a arrumar a nossa casa, o Brasil. Mas sei que ainda há muito a ser feito. Estou escutando o clamor legítimo e urgente de vocês por mudanças, por segurança, por futuro e prosperidade. Estou comprometido com a melhoria da saúde pública, para que sua família fique bem cuidada; com o aumento real da renda, com poder de compra; e com a preservação da natureza criada por Deus. O Brasil é nosso! Eu vou escutar e atender aos anseios de vocês. Sei que, nas famílias evangélicas, tudo se decide em oração. Por isso, conclamo vocês a pedirem discernimento a Deus para fazer a escolha nesta eleição. Vá às urnas com a consciência livre e com a aliança renovada com o nosso amado Brasil. Com gratidão por sua atenção e generosa leitura, conto com suas orações e sigo olhando firmemente para a esperança da vitória e de um Brasil mais justo, respeitoso e com oportunidades para todos."

articles.title: Caso Master: STF acelera análise antes da posse do novo Senado | G1
articles.standfirst: Setores do Supremo acreditam que, se o STF não tomar uma decisão sobre o material, a nova composição do Senado irá fazê-lo, ampliando a pressão sobre a Corte.
articles.summary: Edson Fachin orienta triagem no Caso Master para que o STF decida sobre investigações e evite o aumento da pressão política com a nova composição do Senado.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal (PF) vai fazer uma triagem criteriosa das citações a ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), separando referências feitas por terceiros de informações com robustez jurídica que possam justificar uma investigação.

A orientação de Edson Fachin, presidente do Supremo, é produzir um relatório contextualizado, sem juízo de valor, mas com elementos concretos que deem consistência às informações . Ciro Soares, lobista que trabalhava para Vorcaro, está na mira da PF e pode ser investigado por suspeitas de tráfico de influência e de vender suposto acesso a ministros.

Depois da triagem, caberá ao plenário do Supremo decidir o que deve ser investigado ou arquivado.

O objetivo é tentar dar um encaminhamento institucional ao caso, especialmente diante da chegada da nova composição do Senado. O entendimento de setores do Supremo é que, se o STF não tomar uma decisão sobre o material, o Senado irá fazê-lo, ampliando a pressão sobre a Corte.

Esse encaminhamento, porém, não ocorrerá antes do segundo turno das eleições. Não há prazo definido para a conclusão do trabalho.

O STF já esteve diante da chance de dar um desfecho para o caso — ou, pelo menos, um rumo avançado — no dia 15 de setembro. O que não só não ocorreu, como ampliou a crise com acusações mútuas sem encaminhamento jurídico para apurar os casos divulgados envolvendo ministros e o caso Master.

Presidente do STF, Edson Fachin em audiência com Andrei Rodrigues, Diretor-Geral da Polícia Federal — Foto: Gustavo Moreno/STF

articles.title: PEC fim da escala 6x1: Equipe de Lula vê apoio falso de Flávio | G1
articles.standfirst: Flávio teria dito a apoiadores que, se for eleito, vai aprovar outra proposta garantindo aos empresários a negociação por hora trabalhada.
articles.summary: Governo questiona apoio de Flávio Bolsonaro à PEC fim da escala 6x1 e alerta para possíveis mudanças na proposta que beneficiariam apenas os empresários.
articles.body:
Aliados do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmam que a conversão do candidato do PL, Flávio Bolsonaro, à proposta do fim da escala 6x1 é falsa.

Nesta terça-feira (13), depois de visitar o pai, Flávio Bolsonaro declarou apoio à proposta defendida por Lula sob a justificativa de que, andando pelas ruas, ouviu que os trabalhadores querem aprovar a medida.

O ministro das Relações Institucionais, José Guimarães, afirmou ao blog que a conversão do filho do ex-presidente Bolsonaro é falsa.

Segundo ele, se for eleito, o candidato do PL vai aprovar outra proposta garantindo aos empresários a negociação por hora trabalhada em vez da criação do sistema de duas folgas semanais para os trabalhadores.

"Ele mudou de lado por causa da pressão das ruas, mas vai mudar tudo se for eleito", disse o ministro.

O candidato à presidência do Brasil, Flávio Bolsonaro, do Partido Liberal (PL), fala à imprensa, acompanhado de sua esposa, Fernanda Bolsonaro, após uma missa em homenagem a Nossa Senhora Aparecida, antes do segundo turno das eleições, em Brasília, Brasil, em 12 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Herculano

O articulador político de Lula acredita na aprovação da PEC do fim da escala 6x1 em dois turnos nesta quarta-feira (14) e diz que a "conversão repentina" de Flávio Bolsonaro é uma tentativa de reduzir o desgaste maior que seria votar contra a proposta.

O ministro afirmou ainda que o candidato do PL vinha criticando a medida, chamando-a de oportunista e populista, mas que agora, diante do impacto negativo, mudou de lado.

"Quero ver se ele vai estar lá no plenário defendendo de fato a medida e assumindo o compromisso de que não irá mudá-la depois", afirmou o ministro da Articulação Política do presidente Lula.

A PEC será votada ainda nesta quarta-feira. O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre, disse que os líderes do governo já conseguiram as assinaturas necessárias para que os dois turnos sejam aprovados ainda hoje. A medida será usada como munição por Lula nesta reta final da campanha.

articles.title: TSE manda remover vídeo de Nikolas com críticas de crianças a Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão liminar afirma que o conteúdo contém desinformação e "exploração inadequada da inocência infantil". No vídeo, crianças acusam Lula, Lulinha e o PT de crime e tecem críticas voltadas à insegurança, criminalidade, economia e medo do futuro.
articles.summary: TSE ordena remoção de vídeo de Nikolas Ferreira, replicado por Flávio Bolsonaro, com crianças criticando Lula, por considerar a peça desinformação e exploração infantil.
articles.body:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) determinou, nessa terça-feira (13), a remoção em até 24 horas de um vídeo publicado por Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) em que crianças acusam o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) de crime e tecem críticas ao governo federal, ao Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT) e ao filho de Lula, Lulinha.

A peça foi publicada nas redes sociais de Nikolas e replicada no canal de WhatsApp de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que disputa a Presidência com Lula.

O g1 verificou que o vídeo foi removido do Instagram do deputado Nikolas Ferreira e do canal 'Tropa do Flávio', de Flávio Bolsonaro no WhatsApp. Nas contas do deputado nas redes sociais X e Facebook, a publicação ainda estava no ar.

A decisão do ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze Oliveira atendeu a um pedido do PT, que afirmou que a peça leva os eleitores à desinformação, apresentando informações verdadeiras de forma fragmentada ou fora de contexto para induzir a uma conclusão enganosa.

Segundo os advogados do partido, o conteúdo associa artificialmente Lula à ideia de que crianças perdem a infância por causa da violência e de outros problemas sociais.

A defesa do PT argumentou ainda que, ao utilizar crianças, o vídeo potencializa o impacto emocional da mensagem e pode comprometer a dignidade dos menores de idade.

No vídeo, publicado no último dia 12 de outubro, Dia das Crianças, o deputado Nikolas Ferreira mostra crianças que, em trechos editados, fazem críticas ao governo federal.

Uma delas diz que Lula e Lulinha, filho do presidente, seriam responsáveis pelo roubo do dinheiro da avó para comprar uma bicicleta. As críticas feitas pelas crianças ao governo federal, a Lula e ao PT ainda abordam assuntos envolvendo economia, segurança e medo do futuro.

Segundo a decisão do ministro, o vídeo "ultrapassa a barreira do razoável ao tentar atingir o eleitor psicologicamente mediante a abordagem indevida da propaganda negativa a um candidato veiculada massivamente na internet, aproveitando-se da exploração inadequada da inocência infantil".

Deferida em caráter liminar, a decisão será submetida ainda ao plenário do TSE.

Nikolas Ferreira (PL) — Foto: Bruno Spada/Câmara dos Deputados

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro recua e diz que irá ao debate no domingo após Lula confirmar presença | G1
articles.standfirst: Durante evento que formalizou apoio majoritário do MDB ao candidato, Flávio afirmou que não iria ao primeiro debate e avaliaria se iria no da TV Globo.
articles.summary: Durante evento que formalizou apoio majoritário do MDB ao candidato, Flávio afirmou que não iria ao primeiro debate e avaliaria se iria no da TV Globo.
articles.body:
Candidato Flávio Bolsonaro em vídeo — Foto: Reprodução

O senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), publicou um vídeo nesta quarta-feira (14) afirmando que irá ao debate com presidenciáveis marcado para neste domingo (18).

"Bastou eu falar que não ia no debate, para você [Lula], no minuto seguinte, falar que vai no debate. É claro que eu vou no debate, eu só queria que você confirmasse", afirmou o candidato.

Durante evento em São Paulo, nessa terça-feira (13), Flávio disse que faltaria ao debate desta semana e que ainda iria avaliar se comparecerá ao da TV Globo, marcado para 23 de outubro, dois dias antes do segundo turno.

O adversário dele nas urnas, presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), confirmou a presença. Em publicação nas redes sociais, ele afirmou que espera que Flávio compareça.

articles.title: Relatório da PF sobre envolvimento de ministros com Daniel Vorcaro fica para depois da eleição | G1
articles.body:
Em busca de evitar mais turbulência durante o período eleitoral, o relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) sobre o envolvimento de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro será entregue ao presidente da Corte, Edson Fachin, apenas em novembro.

A decisão agrada às duas alas do STF que vinham se digladiando por causa das investigações envolvendo o dono do extinto Banco Master.

O acerto foi feito ontem, durante reunião do diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Passos Rodrigues, com Fachin. No encontro, ficou decidido que a Polícia Federal fará uma análise exaustiva dos nomes de magistrados citados em conversas e mensagens de Vorcaro.

Aqueles sobre os quais forem encontrados elementos que indiquem possíveis irregularidades serão incluídos no relatório.

O documento também será submetido à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), para parecer. Depois, Fachin irá submetê-lo ao plenário do STF.

Na avaliação de investigadores, esse é o caminho correto, porque uma eventual decisão sobre a abertura de investigações contra ministros da Corte deve passar pelo colegiado.

A partir da decisão do plenário, poderão ser autorizadas investigações sobre ministros caso sejam identificados indícios de crime relacionados a Vorcaro.

Segundo ministros e investigadores ouvidos pelo blog , o resultado da eleição também deverá influenciar o ambiente interno do Supremo.

Na avaliação dessas fontes, uma vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro ou do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) produziria cenários distintos na Corte, inclusive para a discussão sobre eventuais investigações.

Nos bastidores, há ainda a avaliação de que o caso pode acabar arquivado caso prevaleça o entendimento de que os elementos reunidos não são suficientes para justificar a abertura de investigações.

articles.title: White House officials question how long Katie Zacharia can last after 'brutal' press briefing
articles.summary: Several White House officials are questioning how long Katie Zacharia will keep the press secretary job after her first briefing Tuesday, noting her performa...
articles.body:
Several White House officials are questioning how long Katie Zacharia will keep the press secretary job after her first briefing Tuesday, saying her performance was unlikely to satisfy President Donald Trump.

Several advisers and officials offered negative reviews of the briefing to CNN, with one characterizing it as "brutal." Others described it as unusual, awkward, stilted and, at times, uncomfortable. Zacharia appeared at the podium for only about 15 minutes, and most of that time was dedicated to an opening statement touting Trump's accomplishments. She called on only three reporters for questions before ending the briefing.

Some White House officials and Trump advisers expressed confusion about why the White House rushed Zacharia to the podium. A source familiar with the matter said Trump had asked Zacharia to conduct the briefing, and while some in his orbit had misgivings, the source was unaware of anyone relaying them to Zacharia or Trump.

"She should have been doing murder boards for two weeks before going up there," one Trump adviser told CNN, before critiquing Zacharia's performance. "The best thing she did was break the news about [Ambassador to Greece Kimberly] Guilfoyle — at least that takes the focus off of her performance."

"Why did they put her out there so quickly?" a White House official said incredulously. "Literally zero reason to put her out on her second day, unprepared."

Trump praised Zacharia after the briefing, telling reporters shortly after: "I thought she was very good." White House communications director Steven Cheung also said in a statement to CNN that "Katie is a fabulous and wonderful addition to the team."

Zacharia planned ahead of time that she would give lengthy introductory remarks, based on what Trump had requested, and take only take three questions – from outlets she chose ahead of time, a source familiar with the matter said.

The briefing was notably shorter than what had become the norm. Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt's briefings lasted for about an average of 45 minutes. During her first briefing, she called on two "new media" reporters before an Associated Press correspondent. She would also take questions from reporters standing in the aisles.

Zacharia called on reporters from conservative outlet Breitbart, which was in the "new media" seat, Fox News and the Daily Mail. She appeared to have their names written down ahead of time.

Trump and Zacharia met briefly ahead of the briefing, and Trump told her he was seeking Guilfoyle's resignation, a source said.

Another adviser told CNN that while Zacharia "wasn't great," it was just her first press briefing. They expected Trump would give her the benefit of the doubt.

Trump had grown somewhat infatuated with Zacharia's appearances on Fox News before eventually hiring her, sources told CNN. But one of the advisers noted that appearing on a cable TV panel and standing in front of the world at the podium were two different things.

"No question we're all missing Karoline," said one adviser.

Zacharia said she was cutting the briefing short because Trump would likely soon take reporter questions on the White House South Lawn before he departed for Alaska.

"I am going to end it because President Trump is heading out to Marine One for our historic trip to Alaska, and we can ask him all of the questions out there," she said.

Questions have also surfaced online about Zacharia's status as an attorney , and CNN has found no evidence that she has passed the bar exam in the states where she has lived and worked since graduating Pepperdine Caruso School of Law. When Trump announced her new role, he referred to his new press secretary as "an attorney."

"The State Bar of California has no record of Kate Sharon Zacharia or Kate Sharon Black having been licensed to practice law in California," a spokesperson for the California State Bar told CNN in a statement, referring to her maiden name. "Due to confidentiality requirements, the State Bar can only confirm whether someone passed the bar exam, not whether they took the bar exam."

When a reporter pressed Trump at the White House on Tuesday morning about what state Zacharia passed the bar exam in, the president turned to his new press secretary, who was standing behind him.

"Which state?" Trump asked Zacharia. She responded that she had moved to China.

In response to questions on her legal credentials, a White House official told CNN that Zacharia moved to China with her husband after graduating law school, citing his job at an American private equity firm, and that she worked on international transaction law at the time. The official did not respond to a follow-up question about whether she passed the bar exam.

According to her LinkedIn profile, Zacharia worked as an associate on the international practice team at Zhong Lun Law in Beijing from August 2011 to June 2013. She was also general counsel to Fix California , an elections-focused nonprofit founded by Trump ally Ric Grenell, from January 2024 to March 2025. Her most recent position was senior communications adviser for the Trump Media and Technology Group.

It is unclear on what cadence Zacharia will brief reporters. A CNN Reliable Sources analysis of the White House video archive found Leavitt, who departed the role in August, held formal briefings about once a week on average before having her second child. She held 14 briefings in the four months leading up to her maternity leave in late April.

She held another 49 briefings through the rest of 2025, which included several nontraditional briefings.

This story and headline have been updated with additional reporting.

CNN's Alejandra Jaramillo contributed to this report.

articles.title: Federal appeals court rules some nonviolent felons can legally own guns
articles.summary: The Third Circuit ruled a federal felon gun ban applies to violent offenders but not a man whose conviction stemmed from a DUI in the early 2000s.
articles.body: A federal appeals court on Tuesday ruled that a federal ban on gun possession by convicted felons cannot be constitutionally applied to some people whose prior offenses did not involve violence or threats indicating a risk of misusing firearms. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit issued two rulings clarifying when the federal prohibition on gun possession by convicted felons can be enforced under the Second Amendment. The court, which includes several judges appointed by President Donald Trump, upheld the firearms restriction against a man with a conviction stemming from a carjacking but ruled that the ban could not be applied to another man based on his prior drunk-driving convictions. One of the cases decided on Tuesday involved James Bost, who pleaded guilty to terroristic threats, criminal conspiracy, false imprisonment and simple assault in Pennsylvania state court following a 2002 carjacking. MAJOR APPEALS COURT DECLARES NEW JERSEY AR-15 BAN UNCONSTITUTIONAL IN LANDMARK SECOND AMENDMENT RULING Bost was later indicted on federal firearms charges after authorities found him in possession of a gun despite his prior convictions. He sought to dismiss the charges, arguing that the federal ban violated his Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms. U.S. Circuit Judge Stephanos Bibas, writing for the majority in the decision against Bost, said people convicted of crimes demonstrating a risk of physical violence through the misuse of firearms may presumptively be disarmed based on those convictions alone. "The right to keep and bear arms has limits, and this is one: Those who pose a risk of physical violence from misusing guns can be disarmed before that risk becomes a reality," wrote Bibas, an appointee of President Donald Trump. In a separate case involving Edward Williams, the court ruled that the federal firearms restriction could not constitutionally be applied to him based on his prior convictions for driving under the influence of alcohol in the early 2000s. One of those convictions triggered the federal ban, which generally applies to offenses punishable by more than one year in prison. Williams had been sentenced to a term of 90 days to two years, which he served under home confinement. After learning the conviction prevented him from owning guns, he sued to secure a declaration that the law was unconstitutional as applied to his offense. Writing for the court, U.S. Circuit Judge Paul Matey, a Trump appointee, rejected the Justice Department's argument that historical restrictions on "habitual drunkards" justified applying the federal firearms ban to Williams. Matey described Williams as "a peaceable ​citizen, capable of bearing arms consistent with the design of the Second Amendment." "And with that rehabilitation comes restoration of the civic privileges guaranteed to citizens by the Constitution, and the freedom to again exercise the natural right of armed defense against threats and tyranny," the judge wrote. U.S. Circuit Judge Arianna Freeman, writing separately in disagreement with the majority's reasoning, said she parted ways from the majority opinion "when it says a prior conviction is disarming on its face only if it involved violence or threats." DOJ THREATENS TO SUE CALIFORNIA OVER 'GLOCK BAN,' ARGUING LAW VIOLATES SECOND AMENDMENT Freeman argued that the Second Amendment also permits restrictions on people whose criminal conduct demonstrates a credible threat to public safety, even when their offenses did not involve explicit violence or threats. The judge argued that while convictions for crimes that involve violence or threats qualify, other offenses, such as drunk driving, should be covered as well because they show that a person "poses a credible threat to the physical safety of others." Joshua Prince, a lawyer for Williams, praised the ruling, saying the decision made it clear that "there does not exist any historical tradition of stripping individuals with non-violent convictions of their Second Amendment rights and whom do not pose a threat to the public in possession of a firearm." The rulings come amid a series of cases evaluating whether modern gun restrictions are constitutional under a new legal standard established by the Supreme Court's landmark 2022 Second Amendment decision. Bruen, the high court held that modern gun restrictions must be "consistent with this nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation." Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Kamala Harris faces Democratic doubts over 2028 as allies push back on claims she’s squandered her chance
articles.summary: Kamala Harris adviser Maria Cardona fires back at Democratic donors and strategists who say the former vice president blew her chance to reinvent herself.
articles.body: As former Vice President Kamala Harris weighs another White House run in 2028, a longtime advisor is firing back at Democratic strategists and donors who argue she has squandered an opportunity to politically reinvent herself following her 2024 election defeat. Veteran Democratic strategist Maria Cardona, an outside advisor to Harris, pushed back against the criticism highlighted in a new Politico report, defending Harris' policy proposals and campaign activity as Democrats debate whether the former vice president deserves another shot at the White House. Cardona argued the story was "infuriating in its silliness." The report, based on interviews with nearly 20 California-based Democratic donors and strategists, highlighted growing skepticism among some party insiders about Harris' political future and whether she has done enough to distinguish herself from her unsuccessful 2024 campaign. Longtime Democratic strategist Doug Herman, a veteran of former President Barack Obama’s 2008 and 2012 campaigns, told Politico that Harris "totally blew it ... She hasn’t gotten into the mix." AOC GIVES MAJOR HINT ABOUT 2028 Former Gov. Jim Hodges of South Carolina, the lead off state in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nominating calendar, told Politico, "I don’t see anything different myself. It seems like more of the same to me." But Cardona, a veteran of the Bill Clinton administration, the Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama presidential campaigns who currently serves as a member of the Democratic National Committee, disagreed that Harris had failed to spell out what she would offer Democrats anxious for change. "How can you state that she hasn’t done anything new or groundbreaking or talked about new initiatives or policies and then lay out exactly those policies — like proposing an expanded Supreme Court, lowering the voting age to 16, making D.C. and Puerto Rico states. Those are pretty groundbreaking policies!" Cardona told Fox News Digital, as she pointed to some of Harris' moves since the end of former President Joe Biden's administration. Harris, the nation's first Black vice president, has also said that Black people should be "transactional voters," instead of automatically supporting Democratic candidates. "She’s damned if she does and damned if she doesn’t," Cardona argued, adding that Harris "is still the most qualified person to be president of the United States that is mentioned as a possible candidate for 2028." Harris has been crisscrossing the country this year, first on a book tour for her best-selling campaign memoir "107 Days" and currently to support fellow Democrats running in the midterm elections. DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB While Harris has teamed up with Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and congressional nominees in her home state, some Democratic nominees running in red states made headlines in recent weeks by asking the former vice president not to campaign with them. But Cardona said, "Harris has been out there nonstop talking to young voters, women voters, Black voters, Latino voters, and she has been asked by many candidates to come and campaign with them. She has focused her energies on winning the midterm elections. Can you imagine the backlash if she was out there focusing on herself and how she can remake the Democratic Party?" Harris replaced Biden as the Democrats' 2024 presidential nominee after he ended his re-election bid following a disastrous debate performance against President Donald Trump. Her truncated three-month presidential campaign ended in defeat, with Trump narrowly sweeping all the key battleground states as he won back the White House. If she runs a third time for president, Harris will enjoy instant name ID and plenty of goodwill from within her party. But she would also face a Democratic base trying to move past the 2024 election setbacks, and she would likely be part of a very crowded and competitive 2028 primary field. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER A Democratic consultant, who asked for anonymity to speak more freely, told Fox News Digital that "voters feel like they haven't heard much from Harris, which means bad memories from her 2024 election loss remain fresh in their minds." But longtime Democratic strategist Michael Ceraso said that consultants "are not voters." "I just don’t trust that the consulting class really has a finger on the electorate," he told Fox News Digital. "To listen to consultants saying Harris has blown it – presidential politics hasn’t really even started yet. These consultants are just getting soundbites." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ceraso noted that it took Biden three runs to win the White House. "The third time was the charm and everybody said to Biden when he ran the third time, ‘why are you running.’ Well guess what, he ended up becoming the nominee and the president," he said. "Why can’t Harris look at that template and say ‘that can apply to me too.’"

articles.title: Fraudsters robbed America's Main Street. Republicans are making them pay
articles.summary: The SBA suspended 870,000 borrowers linked to an estimated $39 billion in suspected pandemic loan fraud, the largest action in agency history.
articles.body: As the White House's Fraud Ledger shows, the Small Business Administration (SBA) has uncovered more fraud than any other agency. Through Vice President JD Vance's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, the Trump administration is eliminating waste, fraud and abuse at historic rates. When COVID shut down the country, small business owners did everything they could to keep their doors open. They drained their savings, skipped paychecks, and fought to keep employees on the payroll. While small businesses were fighting to survive, fraudsters stole billions from programs meant to keep them afloat. The Biden-Harris administration had years to hold fraudsters accountable. It never did. Under Republican leadership, that era is over. WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD Last month, SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler stood with Vice President Vance in Kansas City, Missouri, and announced the suspension of 870,000 borrowers linked to an estimated $39 billion in suspected pandemic fraud, the largest action of its kind in the agency's history. As chairman of the House Committee on Small Business, I've worked closely with Administrator Loeffler to go after this money and ensure Main Street isn't left high and dry. Every dollar a fraudster took was a dollar a family business didn't get. The Biden-Harris SBA knew COVID fraud was rampant and still failed to act. In 2023, the SBA’s Office of Inspector General estimated that more than $200 billion in pandemic loans may have gone to fraudsters. Agency leadership at the time stated the actual number was closer to $36 billion. When our committee asked then-SBA Administrator Isabella Guzman to explain the $164 billion difference, she refused to testify. So we kept digging. WHITE HOUSE PUSHES 'WATERSHED' FRAUD-FIGHTING REFORM IN CONGRESS AS VANCE CONVENES TASK FORCE Our committee spent 18 months investigating the pandemic loan programs. What we found was deeply disturbing. Rather than fixing its own broken controls, Biden's SBA pointed fingers at the private lenders it worked with. It even floated ending collections on fraudulent loans under $100,000, valued at about $11 billion, because it didn't want to appear to be strong-arming borrowers. Unfortunately, pandemic loans aren't the whole story. Just look at the 8(a) program, which helps disadvantaged small businesses compete for federal contracts. It only works if those firms do the work themselves. Pass-through schemes, in which the winning firm hands the job off to someone else, cheat the very businesses the program was meant to help. In an effort to rein in fraudulent spending, Administrator Loeffler did something nobody had done in nearly 50 years: she audited the entire program. When hundreds of firms refused to hand over their financial records, she moved to kick them out. The SBA has also closed loopholes that let loans be issued in the names of children and the deceased, some of whom are listed as being older than 115. House Republicans have helped lead this recovery from the start, and are ensuring these reforms stick. In June, the House passed my COVID Fraud Transparency Act, which requires the SBA's inspector general to report quarterly to Congress on COVID loan fraud. My committee also advanced pragmatic anti-fraud bills, including Republican Pennsylvania Rep. Dan Meuser's Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act and my bipartisan Put America on Commission Act. I've spent my career in the car business, and I know that paying commissions delivers results. My bill, the Put America on Commission Act, would reward Americans who come forward with credible tips about pandemic loan fraud, funded by penalties paid by convicted fraudsters. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP When I became chairman, I said we would not write this money off. Democrats spent four years ignoring this fraud and were ready to forgive billions of dollars. House Republicans, alongside Administrator Loeffler and Vice President Vance, will continue pursuing it so that the next time mom-and-pop shops need help, they won't have to stand in line behind fraudsters.

articles.title: Omar raid draws ominous warning from Vance as he blasts progressive rep's 'rage' toward America
articles.summary: JD Vance says the Trump administration won't interfere in the DOJ investigation into Ilhan Omar but warns unprecedented steps may follow if fraud is found.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: TYLER, Texas — Vice President JD Vance told Fox News Digital on Tuesday that the Trump administration has no plans to "butt in" on a Department of Justice (DOJ) investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., after the raid on her Washington, D.C., home the day prior. Vance, however, insisted that the law will be enforced if immigration fraud is uncovered. "We don't want to be like the Biden administration. We never want to be like that — where they would allow the law to go after their political opponents," the vice president said in an exclusive interview following a midterm campaign rally in the Lone Star State on Tuesday. "We really want to let the law, the facts drive this," he continued. "And if justice requires something else be done, then, of course, we'll take a step when we have to." Omar's Washington, D.C., home was subject to a predawn raid on Monday conducted by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the principal investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), as first reported by Fox News Digital. DEMOCRATS' FURY OVER ILHAN OMAR RAID DRAWS STINGING GOP REMINDER ABOUT RAID FROM THE PAST: ‘SET THE PRECEDENT’ Conservatives repeatedly accused then-President Joe Biden's DOJ of politically persecuting President Donald Trump and his allies after his first term in office ended. Most notably for critics, Trump's Mar-a-Lago home was infamously raised by the FBI as part of an investigation into alleged mishandling of classified documents. That case was closed when Trump again won the presidency in 2024. "In the Trump administration, unlike the previous administration, we let the facts and the law drive this stuff — so the president and I really don't butt ourselves in the DOJ investigations," Vance said. "We're not trying to micromanage this. We're not trying to tell [Attorney General] Todd Blanche to do one thing or another. We try to let the facts drive this thing." "So we're gonna let the investigation unfold," he went on before warning: "If, of course, criminal wrongdoing is discovered or potentially fraudulent immigration is uncovered, then obviously there will be legal proceedings to follow that." While an investigation into potential immigration fraud related to a sitting member of Congress is unprecedented, Vance reiterated that authorities will go where the facts take them — no matter the circumstances of the case. "I think we have to let the facts and the law drive this, right? So I don't think you can say because politics might be difficult or politics might be easy, you can't follow the law. You have to actually enforce the law as it exists," he said. COULD TRUMP REVOKE ILHAN OMAR'S CITIZENSHIP FOR ALLEGED BROTHER MARRIAGE? EX FEDERAL PROSECUTOR BREAKS IT DOWN Additionally, the vice president slammed Omar for what he views as a negative attitude towards the United States despite it being the country where her family fled to escape civil war in Somalia in 1991. "And to the question of it being unprecedented, I mean, what I'd say is that Ilhan Omar herself is a very unprecedented person," he said. "We have very rarely had a person in Congress who seems to have such disdain and such rage at the country that gave her a better life," Vance said. "Now, that's not a crime." "But we're going to see whether she did commit a crime. And if she did, we're obviously going to follow the law," he reiterated. Vance made the comments after rallying on behalf of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton at the Tyler Pounds Regional Airport in Tyler, Texas, a city about 100 miles east of Dallas. Paxton is running in a neck-and-neck race with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico just three weeks before Election Day, as Republicans fight desperately to hold control of Congress. ILHAN OMAR'S WEALTH SCANDAL TAKES A TURN JUST ONE DAY AFTER RAID OF HER DC HOME Omar responded to the raid on social media Monday afternoon, both from her personal and government X accounts. "I’m ok," Omar wrote on her own X account hours after the search. "Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement." "For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," she continued. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced." TRUMP RALLY CROWD CHANTS 'DEPORT' AS PRESIDENT RIPS ILHAN OMAR AFTER FEDERAL RAID In a post from her official government X account from just after 1:30 p.m., Omar elaborated further. "This raid by Trump’s DHS is an outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies. For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back," she said. "Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Omar's office for comment, but did not hear back before publication.

articles.title: Republicans in historically critical battleground county pull no punches in midterm homestretch: 'Lot of hope'
articles.summary: Jon Husted targets Sherrod Brown's 50-year political record as the Ohio Senate race tightens around data centers and affordability concerns.
articles.body: HAMILTON, OH - Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is fighting for his political future in a tight race in reliably red Ohio, and he spoke to Fox News Digital along with other local Republicans about what to expect in the few weeks before the critical midterm election. "Look, he's been there for 50 years and everywhere I go, no one can name a single thing that he ever did for them," Husted said about his Democratic opponent Sherrod Brown, who is attempting to return to the U.S. Senate after being defeated by Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, in 2024. "And think about this, you can't keep sending the same old Sherrod Brown back to Washington and expect different results. The place is broken. He's the one that broke it. He created the system. If you wanna see a better, brighter future, you can’t send the same ol' Sherrod Brown back." Husted, speaking to Fox News Digital at a Butler County GOP event on Saturday, pointed to the recent Ohio visits from President Trump, Vice President Vance, and Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., as a sign the momentum is on his side in a race some polls show him trailing. TRUMP TOUTS ‘GOLDEN AGE’ AT OHIO RALLY, URGES VOTERS TO DELIVER GOP MIDTERM WINS "We're seeing a ton of energy and literally in the last month, you can just feel it change…we're just seeing people all around the state just rallying and the crowds have been larger and more enthusiastic than I expected in a midterm. So it gives us a lot of hope." Despite Ohio’s Republican lean, Husted faces an uphill battle in a race that has tightened considerably and Republicans are also contending with the traditional midterm headwinds facing the party in power, making turnout and voter enthusiasm especially critical in the weeks ahead. Republicans are also facing concerns over gas prices and affordability, with voters focused on the cost of everyday essentials ahead of the midterm elections. Fox News Digital asked Husted about those concerns and whether part of his message to voters is that the Democratic Party being put back in power won’t fix those issues. SCHUMER PREACHES AFFORDABILITY IN DEM MIDTERM PITCH WHILE SABOTAGING GOP FIXES FOR SOARING COSTS "Yeah, look, it's common sense versus crazy," Husted explained. "Look, we've done some good things. We have more jobs in Ohio than we've ever had in our history, the lowest unemployment rate. Now we just got to fight to get prices down. The Democrats block us at every turn trying to do that." Democrats in the Senate recently blocked Husted’s legislation aimed at requiring large data centers to pay for the power generation and infrastructure needed to serve their facilities rather than shifting that burden onto taxpayers as the data center issue becomes a top issue on the Ohio campaign trail. "They blocked my ratepayer protection pledge, which would have forced data centers to pay their own way. Why? Because they just wanted to use it as a political issue rather than actually solving problems for people," Husted said. Husted continued, "We're the party of drill, baby drill. They're the part of closing down pipelines and refineries and power plants. We are going to create the energy supply to meet the demand and help lower prices. The Democrats, they don't believe in any of it. They believe in command and control of the government. They want to take more of your money out of your paycheck, send it to Washington. If you want your freedom and your fortune, then you need to vote for Republicans." If Husted is going to be successful in November, Ohio attorney and political strategist Mehek Cooke says the key will be pushing back hard on the affordability issue. "I think Senator Houston every single day needs to close that deal by talking about his ratepayer protection data plan, where he promised to cut costs for every single American by saying data centers will not take our resources, taxpayers will not pay for those bills, data centers will and every Democrat voted against that," Cooke said, adding that the vote against Husted’s bill shows Democrats "don’t care about data centers." "You know what they care about? The money that data centers give them," Cooke said, referencing Fox News Digital reporting that Brown has taken money from companies that operate data centers. "Jekyll and Hyde, I've said this about Sherrod," Cooke said. "He's a different man in Ohio. He's the aw shucks, I'm disheveled, I don't know where I am, what day is it? You love me, I love you. And then he gets to Washington and he turns his back on us. So we care about datacenters. We don't wanna pay their bills. And guess what? John Husted will make sure we never do. He's pushing affordability that Sherrod Brown could never dream of while pocketing their money." Brown campaign spokesperson Lauren Chou pushed back in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing Husted of supporting the war in Iran that "sent the costs of gas and diesel to record highs" and saying he "led the charge to bring 226 data centers to Ohio." "Jon Husted puts corporations and billionaires first every time, and we all pay for it," Chou said. Butler, Clermont and Warren counties form a critical Republican vote reservoir in southwestern Ohio, collectively producing hundreds of thousands of votes and some of the state’s largest GOP margins. Their importance was underscored in 2004, when George W. Bush’s combined margin in the three counties exceeded his statewide margin of victory. RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION Several Republican candidates on stage Saturday night pointed to the importance of those counties and Art Sauerwein, Butler County GOP Executive Committee Chairman, told Fox News Digital the "biggest concern" he’s hearing from Republicans is that if Democrats win the governorship, Senate seat, and contested House races "our state’s going to be in huge trouble." "The wokeness that's been going on under the Democrat leadership has really damaged Ohio in the past and we have our platform as Republicans to cut taxes, cut spending, eliminate fraud and waste and we want to work on our schools and get the wokeness that's in our schools," Sauerwein said, adding that Republicans are "energized and motivated." Billionaire entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy also appears to be in a neck-and-neck race with his Democratic opponent, former Ohio Department of Health Director Amy Acton. Sauerwein expressed optimism about that race, calling Ramaswamy the "hardest working guy I have seen." His message is spectacular to what we need in Ohio. If he only delivers on half of what he says, Ohio is going to be in awesome shape."

articles.title: Democrats have ‘dirty hands’ over complaints about Omar raid weeks before election, ex-prosecutor says
articles.summary: Former federal prosecutors say the Justice Department's 60-day rule that Democrats cite in the Ilhan Omar home search is unwritten, not a ban.
articles.body: Former federal prosecutors are pushing back on Democrats' accusations that the Trump administration violated Justice Department policy by searching the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., just weeks before an election. "It's difficult to not point out the dirty hands of the people that might complain about election interference," Jim Trusty, a former federal prosecutor, said, pointing to former special counsel Jack Smith's prosecution of President Donald Trump ahead of the 2024 election. "Democrats definitely can't contend that it's a politicized investigation after everything that happened in the Trump era," Abhishek Kambil, a former federal prosecutor, told Fox News Digital. Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, released a lengthy statement alleging that the Justice Department violated protocol by conducting "overt actions in politically-sensitive matters in the 60 days before an election." HOMAN CONFIRMS 'CRIMINAL' INVESTIGATION INVOLVING ILHAN OMAR, SAYS HE KNOWS 'THINGS ARE GOING ON’ "Just 22 days before the elections, this is blatant political intimidation and an attempt to interfere with the Congresswoman’s reelection," Raskin wrote in his press release. But Kambil pointed out that the U.S. Department of Justice Manual, which outlines procedures for federal criminal investigations, does not explicitly impose a 60-day period before elections in which investigative actions can't be conducted. "The 60-day requirement is not something that's in the justice manual," Kambil told Fox News Digital. "That's basically an unwritten practice of what DOJ typically does, and the justice manual itself does not have the time frame on that." Kambil said that any actions which could be perceived as influencing an election will require prior approval from either the attorney general or the deputy attorney general. The Justice Department has long followed an unwritten practice known as the "60-day rule," which discourages politically sensitive investigative actions close to an election. The practice came under scrutiny in a 2018 DOJ inspector general report examining former FBI Director James Comey's decision to notify Congress of new developments in the Hillary Clinton email investigation just 11 days before the 2016 presidential election. The watchdog concluded that Comey had disregarded longstanding department policy and practice, calling his decision a "serious error of judgment." "It doesn't create a ban; it just creates effectively a consultation requirement to higher level leadership before it can happen, but there is no statute or anything else preventing this," Kambil told Fox News Digital. The Justice Department also was accused by President Donald Trump of ignoring its "60-day rule" when special counsel Jack Smith filed a revised indictment against Trump just 70 days before the 2024 presidential election. Weeks later, Smith submitted a 165-page brief outlining evidence against Trump in the federal election interference case, which was made public just 34 days before the election. Trump and Republican lawmakers accused Smith of attempting to influence the election, but Smith maintained that his office followed DOJ policy and complied with a court-ordered filing schedule. "For 60 days prior to an election, the Department of Injustice is supposed to do absolutely nothing that would taint or interfere with a case," Trump posted in all capital letters to his Truth Social. "They disobeyed their own rule in favor of complete and total election interference." BIDEN-ERA FBI’S ‘NIXONIAN’ TRUMP FAMILY SURVEILLANCE DRAWS SCRUTINY FROM UNLIKELY CORNER "Going back to Jack Smith, obviously trying to get a case tried — the January 6th case before the election — to affect the electorate," Trusty said. Trusty pointed out that the Justice Department needed approval from a magistrate judge in Washington, D.C., before executing its search warrant. "There's at least probable cause," Trusty said. "It's a long way off from proving a case at trial." "But keep in mind, in D.C. President Trump and his administration don't always have friendly treatment from the judges there," Trusty continued. "So this was a magistrate judge who looked at the sworn statement, said there's enough to justify a raid, and now we've had a raid." A judge can reject a search warrant application if investigators fail to establish probable cause. But approving a warrant does not necessarily resolve questions about whether the search complied with the Justice Department's election-year policies. TRUMP DOJ UNLEASHES LARGEST DENATURALIZATION EFFORT IN DEPARTMENT HISTORY — AND SAYS IT’S ‘ONLY THE BEGINNING’ "When you see Democrats challenging the warrant or what happened, they're not really going after the merits," Kambil said. "They're challenging the timing." The Homeland Security Investigations raid stems from an investigation into immigration paperwork Omar's father completed when she was a child. Omar, who fled Somalia's civil war, immigrated to the United States with her family in 1995 at age 12 and became a naturalized U.S. citizen in 2000. In response to the raid on her home, Omar accused Trump of engaging in "political intimidation" against her. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "This raid by Trump’s DHS is an outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies," Omar posted on X. "For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back." articles.title: Schumer warns of Republican advantage that could change the battle for Senate control
articles.summary: Senate Democrats face a Republican money tsunami as Chuck Schumer warns colleagues that massive GOP spending could overwhelm their candidates.
articles.body: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer sees a path to victory for Democrats in November — but one major Republican advantage has him worried. In a letter to his Democratic colleagues, Schumer, D-N.Y., argued that his crop of candidates and Democrats running across the country are winning the messaging battle against the GOP, but asked, "Can Republicans buy the Senate?" "With just three weeks until Election Day, the battle for control of the Senate comes down to one defining question: Will the unprecedented tsunami of Republican money defeat the massive Democratic advantage in candidates, policies, and political climate," Schumer wrote. DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS "There are 22 days until Election Day, and two enormous forces are on a collision course: deep voter dissatisfaction with Republicans and an unprecedented flood of money aimed at overcoming their political liabilities," he continued. "Which force prevails could determine control of the United States Senate." Republicans do have a distinct money advantage and have seen outside groups and President Donald Trump’s MAGA Inc. spending at eye-popping levels across the Senate map. MAGA Inc., for example, has over $400 million at its disposal, according to Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings, and reportedly has plans to spend in key Senate races like Iowa, Ohio and Alaska in the waning weeks of the midterms. SUPREME COURT STRIKES DOWN LIMIT ON PARTY CAMPAIGN SPENDING IN COORDINATION WITH CANDIDATES Then there’s tech billionaire Elon Musk, who has contributed roughly $276 million to Republican-aligned political action committees (PACs) this cycle. Notably, he contributed $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, a super PAC closely aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D. Schumer lamented the funding, arguing that it was coming from a small field of deep-pocketed donors "looking to buy a pardon, curry favor, and move the needle in favor of their personal interests." He also charged that the influx of cash was thanks in part to the Supreme Court’s decision in June to eliminate federal limits on how much political parties can spend on candidates. DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT "None of us are naïve; we’ve known this day would come ever since Justices Kennedy, Roberts, Scalia, Alito, and Thomas decided to give their billionaire and corporate friends permission to buy elections," Schumer said. But Democrats’ own super PAC, the Senate Majority PAC, which is closely aligned with Schumer, broke its own fundraising records in the third quarter of this year, raking in $151 million. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) announced shortly after the court’s decision that it would be pumping in $40 million in a slew of battleground states. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And the Senate GOP’s campaign arm, the National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC), also teed up over $46 million in battleground races. "This pity pitch from Chuck Schumer is a testament to the enthusiasm of Republican grassroots donors who are re-engaging in full force to stop Democrats’ socialist march," NRSC spokeswoman Bernadette Breslin told Fox News Digital. "Unfortunately for Schumer, the DNC’s debt crisis is symptomatic of a dying Democratic brand, with approval ratings in the toilet and donors doubting their own chances of flipping the Senate."

articles.title: Supreme Court case pits 1980s video rental law versus modern newsletters
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday will examine the reach of a decades-old privacy law designed to protect video rental records in a case that could shape current and future lawsuits over digital tracking tools. The justices are weighing whether the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) protects consumers who subscribe to any of a company’s products or only those…
articles.body:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday will examine the reach of a decades-old privacy law designed to protect video rental records in a case that could shape current and future lawsuits over digital tracking tools.

The justices are weighing whether the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) protects consumers who subscribe to any of a company’s products or only those who subscribe to its audiovisual ones.

The case arises from a class-action lawsuit brought against Paramount Global in 2022 by Michael Salazar, a subscriber to a 247Sports.com newsletter. The website is a hub for college sports and recruiting news that offers dozens of daily newsletters to its subscribers.

Salazar alleges that Paramount has violated the VPPA by installing a Facebook tracking pixel on the website that allowed his data, including video viewing history, to be shared without his consent. That information was then used for targeted advertising.

The VPPA makes a “video tape service provider” liable for damages when it knowingly discloses a consumer’s personally identifiable information without written consent. It was enacted in response to the leak of failed Supreme Court nominee Robert Bork’s video rental history to the press during his confirmation process.

At issue is whether Salazar fits into the VPPA’s definition of a “consumer,” which is classified as “any renter, purchaser, or subscriber of goods or services from a video tape service provider.”

Salazar argues he does, while Paramount claims he doesn’t.

A federal judge in Tennessee found that Salazar’s subscription did not qualify him as a “consumer” under the law because the newsletter was not “audio visual materials” and dismissed the complaint. A divided panel for the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals later affirmed that ruling.

Salazar appealed to the Supreme Court, asking the justices to resolve a circuit split over how to interpret the statutory language.

“There is simply no basis to rewrite the VPPA’s definition of ‘consumer’ to impose a limitation that appears nowhere in the text,” his lawyer Joshua Hammack wrote in a brief.

Lawyers representing Paramount argued in their brief that the term should be read narrowly, warning that accepting Salazar’s view that it applies to all goods and services could open the floodgates of litigation.

“Salazar’s contrary reading would transform a 1988 video-rental statute into an unworkable internet-privacy regime of broad yet incoherent scope backed by harsh penalties,” they wrote. “Statutory protection for viewers of free video content would turn on the happenstance of where they purchased a chicken sandwich or recliner years earlier.”

A decision in the case is expected by next summer.

articles.title: Surprise Russia diesel deal spurned by growing number of GOP senators
articles.summary: A growing number of Senate Republicans are criticizing President Trump’s surprise deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import 2.2 million tons of Russian diesel into the U.S. market. At least eight Republican senators have expressed public concerns over the deal, which would pave the way for the United States to import hundreds of thousands…
articles.body:
A growing number of Senate Republicans are criticizing President Trump’s surprise deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import 2.2 million tons of Russian diesel into the U.S. market.

At least eight Republican senators have expressed public concerns over the deal, which would pave the way for the United States to import hundreds of thousands of metric tons of Russian diesel over the next two months.

Trump declared on Truth Social that the “highly successful discussion” with Putin will result in rapidly falling diesel prices, but Republican senators are warning the impact on the economy will be “negligible” while voicing skepticism about whether it will materialize at all.

GOP Sens. Mitch McConnell (Ky.), John Cornyn (Texas) and Alan Armstrong (Okla.) on Tuesday joined other GOP senators critical of the diesel deal by signing a letter to Trump calling it “a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our allies.”

The bipartisan letter, which Sens. Thom Tillis (N.C.), Susan Collins (Maine) and Lisa Murkowski (Alaska) also signed, urged Trump to rescind the deal and predicted it would have a “negligible” impact on fuel prices.

“The deal you struck with President Vladimir Putin on October 9th will not achieve just ends, nor will it benefit Americans,” they warned, predicting that lifting sanctions on Russian diesel “only provides Putin with more fuel to finance his war machine and enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians.”

Democratic Sens. Richard Blumenthal (Conn.), Jeanne Shaheen (N.H.), Dick Durbin (Ill.), Sheldon Whitehouse (R.I.), Jack Reed (R.I.) and Chris Coons (Del.) also signed the letter.

The lawmakers warned that allowing U.S. dollars to flow to Russia would “undoubtedly finance its desired war of attrition and advance its security cooperation with China, Iran and North Korea.”

They said the funding could even “endanger servicemembers operating overseas in support of Operation Epic Fury,” referring to the military conflict with Iran.

The Middle East Institute in June reported that Moscow has provided Tehran with satellite targeting data for strikes on U.S. forces. Russia also has provided Iran with fiber-optic drone technology and amplified Iranian propaganda, it said.

“I wasn’t overly delighted with the deal on diesel, and I think there’s not a very high likelihood that it will actually be consummated and be enacted,” Senate Armed Services Committee Chair Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) said at the Warsaw Security Forum. “I think there’s a much better way in the near term to lower energy prices and also to provide some security.”

Economic experts say Trump’s deal to immediately import 2.2 million tons of Russian diesel would supply less than a day’s worth of the nation’s diesel consumption.

“The announced release of fuel is a drop in the bucket in terms of U.S. domestic demand and even less in terms of global demand. It may not even be new supply on the global market. Russian product often gets out,” said Neale Mahoney, an economics professor at Stanford University.

“Any energy economist would agree that it would have a negligible impact on the prices we face domestically and we’re seeing that right now in the markets. Prices for diesel haven’t really noticeably decreased since the announcement,” he said.

The national average price of diesel is now $6.28 per gallon, about 25 cents lower than the high mark of $6.53 per gallon in September.

A former senior Republican Senate staffer said the deal came as a shocking development without a clear strategic gain for the United States.

“The Russia diesel deal makes no sense politically. It won’t bring down fuel prices before the midterms and only reminds voters that Trump hasn’t ended the Ukraine war as he said he would on Day 1,” the former senior GOP aide said.

The aide said Republican senators are now paying a political price for not pushing back harder against Trump earlier this year when he launched the conflict against Iran without prior consultation or advance notification with members of Congress.

“The Iran war is what sent fuel prices soaring, and they are toxic for the Republican brand going into the midterms,” the former senior GOP aide said.

“Senate Republicans have only themselves to blame for failing to ask questions back in February about the war and about who the hell convinced the president it was a good idea to go in there with no endgame,” the source added.

A White House spokesperson said the president’s diesel deal will “help lower prices for farmers, truckers, and families across the nation.”

“President Trump is always willing to look anyone in the eye to deliver wins for the American people – which has resulted in historic trade agreements with countries around the world and major investments into our economy,” said Anna Kelly, the White House spokesperson.

She said the president is “simultaneously” urging “both sides of the Russia-Ukraine conflict to stop strikes against refineries, which are driving up costs and hurting American consumers.”

Collins, Murkowski, Tillis and Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah) issued a joint statement with Democratic colleagues on Sunday notifying Trump that Congress “explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine.”

The senators argued that Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports into the United States ran “directly counter” to the 2022 law because the president “failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation to justify its decision as required by statute.”

Few Republican senators are speaking up to defend the deal, though one Trump ally, Sen. Bill Hagerty (Tenn.), told reporters Tuesday at the Capitol that Trump is putting the nation first.

“I think that the president’s got energy security and economic security front-of-mind right now. He’s focused on Americans first,” Hagerty said.

Pressed on whether the decision to allow an estimated $400 million in new revenue to flow to Russia is wise at a time when Russian forces continue to strike Ukrainian energy infrastructure and civilian targets, Hagerty noted other sanctions remain in place.

“Certainly, we’ve got a number of sanctions in place and a number of efforts to bring Putin into alignment,” he said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Russia violated a ceasefire by striking at least six energy targets across Ukraine.

He warned that allowing Russia to collect more revenue from energy sales would fund “its war machine.”

The Republican senators who signed the bipartisan letter to Trump on Tuesday urged him to withdraw the Treasury Department’s general license to allow Russian diesel imports into the country and instead use the authorities under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act to tighten sanctions on countries that buy Russian energy products.

“These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China, and thereby enhance your negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict,” they wrote.
